A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 14-page versions of WeakMCN. Their text, equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendix A are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original WeakMCN benchmark results, semi-supervised evaluations, ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative analyses in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendix A, including quantitative comparisons and failure cases.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same dual-branch architecture, anchor-text contrastive learning, SAM-generated pseudo masks, DVFE feature combination, and CCM losses. Training objectives and inference procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate referring expression comprehension and segmentation on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg under the same weakly supervised and semi-supervised scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the corresponding experiments, including RefCLIP, APL, and PPT in Table 1; RefTeacher and SemiRes in Table 5; the direct-SAM alternative in Table 6; and efficiency comparators in Table 10.

E3.justification: The reported splits, model configurations, preprocessing, metrics, and training settings are unchanged. Both retain the Google split for weak supervision, IoU@0.5 and mIoU metrics, 416-by-416 inputs, 25 epochs, batch size 64, and the 1% labeled-data protocol.

E4.justification: The component and feature-bank ablations, direct-SAM comparison, ISL-threshold sensitivity, efficiency analyses, and qualitative cases are retained unchanged in Tables 2–4 and 6–10 and Figures 6–7, including Appendix A.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendix. For example, Table 1 retains RefCOCO validation scores of 68.55 for WREC and 58.15 for WRES for WeakMCN with SAM ViT-tiny.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and formulations in Section 3, Equations (1)–(11), are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about joint weakly supervised REC/RES, the contributions of DVFE and CCM, benchmark performance, and generalization to semi-supervised settings.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of task collaboration, feature redundancy, and efficiency tradeoffs. Appendix A.2 preserves the limitations involving overlapping objects, oversegmentation, and difficulty grounding complex, lengthy expressions.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 preserves the encoder specifications, feature dimensions, optimizer settings, and loss weights. Appendix A retains the same parameter counts, training times, and inference speeds, and the code-availability statement and repository link are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 75 references and related-work discussion are retained. The positioning relative to single-task weak supervision and earlier fully supervised multitask approaches is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first two equally contributing authors change from Yang Liu followed by Silin Cheng to Silin Cheng followed by Yang Liu. The first two institutional entries switch numbering/order, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. Body wording and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–10 retain their graphics, content, captions, formatting, and placement. Inspection confirms the same page layout and appendix organization; extraction-spacing differences do not represent substantive visual revisions.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves v1's method, evidence, mathematical formulations, interpretations, and limitations, including all appendix analyses. The author/affiliation-block and version-stamp edits do not establish a meaningful improvement or deterioration in scientific quality, completeness, or readability.
